title: A Short History of Spacecraft Landings on the Moon
credits: The Associated Press reported this story. Bryan Lynn adapted the report for VOA Learning English with additional information from NASA.

sentences.en: Many years have passed since the first spacecraft landed on the moon in 1966.
sentences.zh: 自1966年首艘航天器在月球着陆以来，已过去了许多年。

sentences.en: From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing.
sentences.zh: 从那以后直到现在，人们又进行了许多次尝试，有的成功，有的失败。

sentences.en: Here is a short history of some of these attempts.
sentences.zh: 以下是其中一些尝试的简要历史。

sentences.en: The Soviet Union’s Luna 9 spacecraft was the first to land on the moon.
sentences.zh: 苏联的'月球9号'航天器是首艘在月球着陆的航天器。

sentences.en: It touched down on the lunar surface in 1966.
sentences.zh: 它于1966年降落在月球表面。

sentences.en: The landing came after several other Soviet spacecraft either did not reach the moon or crashed on the surface.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，另有数艘苏联航天器要么未能抵达月球，要么在表面坠毁。

sentences.en: The American space agency NASA says Luna 9 was the first spacecraft to carry out a soft landing on the moon.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局NASA表示，'月球9号'是首艘在月球实现软着陆的航天器。

sentences.en: It was also the first to send “photographic data” from the moon’s surface to Earth.
sentences.zh: 它也是首艘从月球表面向地球发送'影像数据'的航天器。

sentences.en: Luna 9’s landing proved “the lunar surface could support the weight of a lander and that an object would not sink into a loose layer of dust as some models predicted,” NASA said.
sentences.zh: NASA表示，'月球9号'的着陆证明了'月球表面能够承受着陆器的重量，而且物体不会像某些模型所预测的那样陷入松散的尘埃层中。'

sentences.en: In May 1966, the United States followed with its Surveyor 1 mission.
sentences.zh: 1966年5月，美国随后开展了'勘测者1号'任务。

sentences.en: NASA describes this effort as “the first of a series of seven robotic spacecraft sent to the moon to gather data in preparation for NASA's Apollo missions.”
sentences.zh: NASA将此次努力描述为'一系列七艘机器人航天器中的首艘，它们被发射到月球以收集数据，为NASA的'阿波罗'任务做准备。'

sentences.en: The successful soft landing of Surveyor 1 “was one of the great successes of NASA's early lunar and interplanetary program.”
sentences.zh: '勘测者1号'成功的软着陆'是NASA早期月球及行星际项目中的一次重大成功。'

sentences.en: Both the U.S. and Soviet Union had other successful robotic landings.
sentences.zh: 美国和苏联都取得了其他成功的机器人着陆。

sentences.en: Next, the countries aimed to be the first to land humans on the moon.
sentences.zh: 接下来，两国竞相成为首艘将人类送上月球的国度。

sentences.en: In 1969, NASA successfully landed Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the moon.
sentences.zh: 1969年，NASA成功将'阿波罗11号'宇航员尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·奥尔德林送上月球。

sentences.en: The U.S. Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to explore the moon over six missions.
sentences.zh: 美国的'阿波罗'计划在六次任务中先后将12名宇航员送上月球进行探索。

sentences.en: Apollo 17 was the last in 1972.
sentences.zh: '阿波罗17号'是最后一次任务，于1972年进行。

sentences.en: The U.S. is still the only country to land humans on the moon.
sentences.zh: 美国至今仍是唯一将人类送上月球的国度。

sentences.en: NASA officials say the agency’s Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface possibly by the end of 2026.
sentences.zh: NASA官员表示，该局的'阿尔忒弥斯'计划旨在将宇航员重新送上月球表面，可能最早在2026年底实现。

sentences.en: In 2013, China became the third country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon.
sentences.zh: 2013年，中国成为第三家成功将航天器送上月球的国度。

sentences.en: China landed an exploring vehicle, or rover named Yutu that year.
sentences.zh: 那一年，中国成功着陆了一辆名为'玉兔'的探测车。

sentences.en: China followed with the Yutu-2 rover in 2019, this time touching down on the moon’s unexplored far side.
sentences.zh: 2019年，中国又推出了'玉兔二号'探测车，这次着陆在月球从未被探索过的背面。

sentences.en: In 2020, China successfully returned samples of rock and dirt collected by the rovers.
sentences.zh: 2020年，中国成功带回了由探测车采集的岩石和土壤样本。

sentences.en: The mission returned about 1.7 kilograms of lunar material collected from the near side of the moon.
sentences.zh: 这次任务带回了约1.7千克从月球正面采集的月球物质。

sentences.en: Then in 2024, another mission returned rock and soil samples from the less explored far side of the moon.
sentences.zh: 然后在2024年，又一次任务从探索较少的月球背面带回了岩石和土壤样本。

sentences.en: China has said it aims to land its astronauts on the moon by 2030.
sentences.zh: 中国表示，其目标是在2030年前将宇航员送上月球。

sentences.en: In 2023, Russia tried its first moon landing in nearly 50 years.
sentences.zh: 2023年，俄罗斯在近50年来首次尝试月球着陆。

sentences.en: The Luna 25 spacecraft was attempting to land near the lunar south pole.
sentences.zh: '月球-25'航天器试图在月球南极附近着陆。

sentences.en: But it is believed to have crash landed on the moon’s surface.
sentences.zh: 但它被认为撞上了月球表面。

sentences.en: The country’s last effort before that, Luna 24 in 1976, landed successfully and returned moon rocks to Earth.
sentences.zh: 此前该国的最后一次尝试是1976年的'月球-24'，它成功着陆并将月球岩石带回地球。

sentences.en: After its first lander crashed into the moon in 2019, India made its second attempt in 2023.
sentences.zh: 在2019年其首个着陆器撞上月球后，印度在2023年进行了第二次尝试。

sentences.en: The country successfully landed its Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft on the lunar surface.
sentences.zh: 该国成功将'月船三号'航天器降落在月球表面。

sentences.en: The mission made India the fourth nation to complete a moon landing.
sentences.zh: 这次任务使印度成为第四个完成月球着陆的国家。

sentences.en: In January 2024, Japan became the fifth country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon.
sentences.zh: 2024年1月，日本成为第五个成功将航天器降落在月球上的国家。

sentences.en: But the SLIM spacecraft landed upside down.
sentences.zh: 但'SLIM'航天器是倒着陆的。

sentences.en: This caused some power and communication problems, but the lander was able to operate for a short time.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一些电力和通信问题，但着陆器仍能短时间运作。

sentences.en: I’m Bryan Lynn.
sentences.zh: 我是布莱恩·林恩。

glossary.def: an amount of a substance that covers a surface
(space travel) the flight of a spacecraft to perform a certain task or job
a small amount of something that gives you information about the thing it was taken from
